subject: Christian Religious Studies
examFormat: The syllabus aims to develop the social, ethical and moral values of Nigerian youth and candidates who will contribute productively to national development goals; it is organised by themes. The BECE CRS exam has two papers, and candidates answer all questions. Paper 1 has 60 multiple-choice questions (60 marks) drawn from Old Testament themes only: God and His Creation (20), Relationship with God and Man (20) and God's Call (20). Paper 2 has 60 multiple-choice questions (60 marks) on New Testament themes: The Early Life of Jesus Christ, The Ministry of Jesus Christ, The Passion, Death and Resurrection of Jesus Christ, The Beginning of the Church, The Life and Teachings of Paul, and The Christian Church Today (10 questions each); the FAQ states each paper is answered in one hour and there are no essay questions. The 120 marks are weighted at 70%, plus 30% from the school's continuous assessment.
excluded: Ignored the FAQ chapter (used only for the one-hour paper duration and no-essay statement) and the Cultural and Creative Arts / Mathematics text appended after the CRS section of the combined PDF. Bible references are kept as printed, with only OCR artefacts repaired (e.g. 'Mau.'/'Nik.' -> 'Matt.'/'Mk.', 'l Peter' -> '1 Peter', 'IPeL' -> '1 Pet.', 'Judees' -> 'Judges', 'LEI 6:19-31' -> 'Lk. 16:19-31', 'Acts 241' -> 'Acts 2:41', '2626-29' -> '26:26-29'); references truncated in the source are marked with '…' rather than completed. Several references look wrong in the source itself (e.g. Gen. 10:12 for 'Who is God?', Ecc. 17:1, Ruth 11:7-18, Matt. 2:14-30 for the Talents, Matt. 8:1-6 for feeding the four thousand, Lk. 2:51 for qualities of love) but were left unchanged. The theme column shows truncated labels ('HIS CREATION', 'RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND', 'THE PASSION RESURRECTION'); full theme names were taken from the Paper 1/Paper 2 description.

Appearances (Lk. 24:13-49, Matt 28:16-20, Mk 16:9-15, Jn 21:1-14); c. The significance of Jesus' resurrection to Christians.

subtopics.name: The Resurrection
objectives: Narrate the Resurrection (Matt. 28:1-10, Mk. 16:1-8, Lk. 24:1-12)

subtopics.name: Appearances
objectives: Narrate the appearances of the risen Jesus (Lk. 24:13-49, Matt 28:16-20, Mk 16:9-15, Jn 21:1-14)

subtopics.name: Significance of Jesus' resurrection to Christians
objectives: Explain the significance of Jesus' resurrection to Christians

topics.name: The Ascension of Jesus Christ
topics.content: Theme: The Passion, Death and Resurrection of Jesus Christ (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. The Great Commission (Matt. 28:16-20, Mk. 16:15-18); b. Jesus ascends into Heaven (Mk. 16:19-20, Lk 24:50-53); c. Signs that will accompany those who will spread the gospel.

subtopics.name: The Great Commission (Ascension)
objectives: Explain the Great Commission (Matt. 28:16-20, Mk. 16:15-18)

subtopics.name: Jesus ascends into Heaven
objectives: Narrate how Jesus ascended into Heaven (Mk. 16:19-20, Lk 24:50-53)

subtopics.name: Signs that will accompany those who spread the gospel
objectives: State the signs that will accompany those who will spread the gospel

topics.name: The Promise of the Holy Spirit
topics.content: Theme: The Beginning of the Church (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. The Promise of the Holy Spirit (Jn. 14:26, Jn. 15:26, Acts 1:3-5); b. The coming of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:1-13); c. Peter's first speech and its effect (Acts 2:14-41).

subtopics.name: Promise of the Holy Spirit
objectives: Explain the promise of the Holy Spirit (Jn. 14:26, Jn. 15:26, Acts 1:3-5)

subtopics.name: The coming of the Holy Spirit
objectives: Narrate the coming of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:1-13)

subtopics.name: Peter's first speech and its effect
objectives: Explain Peter's first speech and its effect (Acts 2:14-41)

topics.name: Fellowship in the Early Church
topics.content: Theme: The Beginning of the Church (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. Social and religious life of the Early Church: i. togetherness in the Early Church (Acts 2:41-47, 5:1-11); ii. murmuring in the Early Church (Acts 6:1-2); b. Selection of Deacons (Acts 6:1-7), equitable distribution; c. Comparison of the Early Church to present Church.

subtopics.name: Social and religious life of the Early Church
objectives: Describe the social and religious life of the Early Church: togetherness (Acts 2:41-47, 5:1-11) and murmuring (Acts 6:1-2)

subtopics.name: Selection of Deacons
objectives: Narrate the selection of Deacons for equitable distribution (Acts 6:1-7)

subtopics.name: Comparison of the Early Church to the present Church
objectives: Compare the Early Church to the present Church

topics.name: Opposition to the Gospel
topics.content: Theme: The Beginning of the Church (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. Arrest of Peter and John (Acts 3:11-44, 4:5-31); b. Arrest and martyrdom of Stephen (Acts … - 15, 7:1-60); c. Persecution of Church by Saul (Acts … - 31, 9:1-43); d. Martyrdom of James (Acts 12:1-3).

subtopics.name: Arrest of Peter and John
objectives: Narrate the arrest of Peter and John (Acts 3:11-44, 4:5-31)

subtopics.name: Arrest and martyrdom of Stephen
objectives: Narrate the arrest and martyrdom of Stephen (Acts … - 15, 7:1-60)

subtopics.name: Persecution of the Church by Saul
objectives: Describe the persecution of the Church by Saul (Acts … - 31, 9:1-43)

subtopics.name: Martyrdom of James
objectives: Narrate the martyrdom of James (Acts 12:1-3)

topics.name: The Ministry of Peter
topics.content: Theme: The Beginning of the Church (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. Peter and Simon the Magician (Acts 8:14-25); b. Healing miracles of Peter: raising of Dorcas (Acts 9:32 — 42); c. Conversion of Cornelius (Acts 10:1-48): Peter defends his action in Cornelius' house (Acts 11:1 — 18); d. Peter's divine release from prison and death of Herod (Acts 12:1-24).

subtopics.name: Peter and Simon the Magician
objectives: Narrate the story of Peter and Simon the Magician (Acts 8:14-25)

subtopics.name: Healing miracles of Peter
objectives: Narrate the healing miracles of Peter, including the raising of Dorcas (Acts 9:32 — 42)

subtopics.name: Conversion of Cornelius
objectives: Narrate the conversion of Cornelius (Acts 10:1-48) and how Peter defended his action in Cornelius' house (Acts 11:1 — 18)

subtopics.name: Peter's divine release from prison and death of Herod
objectives: Narrate Peter's divine release from prison and the death of Herod (Acts 12:1-24)

topics.name: Some Teachings of St. Paul
topics.content: Theme: The Life and Teachings of Paul (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. Paul's teachings on: i. dignity of labour (2 Thess. 3:6-15, Col. 3:23); ii. obedience to constituted authority (Rom. 13:1-7, Eph. … - 8); iii. love (1 Cor. 13, Rom. 13:8-10); b. Types of work people do; c. Why people should do their work with honour; d. Need to obey the constituted authority (Rom. 13:1-7, Eph 6:5-8).

subtopics.name: Paul's teachings on dignity of labour, obedience and love
objectives: Explain Paul's teachings on dignity of labour (2 Thess. 3:6-15, Col. 3:23), obedience to constituted authority (Rom. 13:1-7, Eph. … - 8) and love (1 Cor. 13, Rom. 13:8-10)

subtopics.name: Types of work people do
objectives: Identify the types of work people do

subtopics.name: Why people should do their work with honour
objectives: Explain why people should do their work with honour

subtopics.name: Need to obey constituted authority
objectives: Explain the need to obey the constituted authority (Rom. 13:1-7, Eph 6:5-8)

topics.name: Paul's Trials
topics.content: Theme: The Life and Teachings of Paul (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. Paul's arrival at Jerusalem and arrest (Acts 21:17 — 40); b. Paul before Jewish Council (Sanhedrin) and the plot to kill him (Acts 22:30-33 and 35); c. Paul before Roman Governors (Felix, Festus and Agrippa) and his appeal to Rome (Acts 25:1-21); Felix: (Acts 24:1-27; Felix (Acts 25:22); Agrippa, Festus: 25, 13-14.

subtopics.name: Paul's arrival at Jerusalem and arrest
objectives: Narrate Paul's arrival at Jerusalem and his arrest (Acts 21:17 — 40)

subtopics.name: Paul before the Jewish Council and the plot to kill him
objectives: Narrate Paul before the Jewish Council (Sanhedrin) and the plot to kill him (Acts 22:30-33 and 35)

subtopics.name: Paul before Roman Governors and his appeal to Rome
objectives: Narrate Paul before the Roman Governors Felix, Festus and Agrippa and his appeal to Rome (Acts 25:1-21; Acts 24:1-27; Acts 25:22; 25, 13-14)

topics.name: The Growth of the Church
topics.content: Theme: The Christian Church Today (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. The Great Commission (Matt. 28:19-20, Mk. 16:15-16); b. Marks of growth in the Church, e.g. organising crusades, revivals, vigils, prayer meetings, miracles etc. (Acts 2:1-47).

subtopics.name: The Great Commission (growth of the Church)
objectives: Explain the Great Commission as a basis for the growth of the Church (Matt. 28:19-20, Mk. 16:15-16)

subtopics.name: Marks of growth in the Church
objectives: Identify marks of growth in the Church, e.g. organising crusades, revivals, vigils, prayer meetings, miracles etc. (Acts 2:1-47)

topics.name: Unity among Christians
topics.content: Theme: The Christian Church Today (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. Christian organisations in Nigeria, e.g. CAN etc.; b. Definition of inter-denomination and their activities; c. Christian giving (Phil. 4:14-20, 2 Cor. … - 5, 2 Cor. 9:6-15); d. Teachings that will foster unity (Jn. 17:15 and 21): i. faith and works (James 2:14— 18); ii. humility (Phil. 2:3— 11); iii. impartiality (James … — 13); iv. forgiveness (Gal. 6:1-2) etc..

subtopics.name: Christian organisations in Nigeria
objectives: Identify Christian organisations in Nigeria, e.g. CAN etc.

subtopics.name: Inter-denomination and their activities
objectives: Define inter-denomination and describe their activities

subtopics.name: Christian giving
objectives: Explain Christian giving (Phil. 4:14-20, 2 Cor. … - 5, 2 Cor. 9:6-15)

subtopics.name: Teachings that will foster unity
objectives: Explain teachings that will foster unity (Jn. 17:15 and 21): faith and works (James 2:14— 18), humility (Phil. 2:3— 11), impartiality (James … — 13), forgiveness (Gal. 6:1-2) etc.

topics.name: Christian Living among Non-Christians
topics.content: Theme: The Christian Church Today (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. Christian living in the community (1 Peter 1:3-17; 2, Matt. 5:13-16); b. Christians' attitude to persecution (1 Peter 1:3-17, James 1:12-15, 1 Peter 1:6-9); c. Discussion on Christians' attitude to non-believing authorities.

subtopics.name: Christian living in the community
objectives: Describe Christian living in the community (1 Peter 1:3-17; 2, Matt. 5:13-16)

subtopics.name: Christians' attitude to persecution
objectives: Explain Christians' attitude to persecution (1 Peter 1:3-17, James 1:12-15, 1 Peter 1:6-9)

subtopics.name: Christians' attitude to non-believing authorities
objectives: Discuss Christians' attitude to non-believing authorities

topics.name: Peaceful Co-existence
topics.content: Theme: The Christian Church Today (Paper 2 (New Testament)). Content: a. Explanation of peaceful co-existence, i.e. living in peace with others (Matt. 5:21-25); instances in the Bible of people desiring peaceful co-existence: i. Esau and Jacob (Gen 31:1-11) (Gen. 13:1-8, 26:26-29); ii. Philemon and Onesimus (Phil. 1:1-30); iii. Isaac and Abimelech (Gen. 26-2 - 29); b. Demonstration of how people can show desire for peaceful co-existence, e.g. call for dialogue, tolerance, forgiveness, reconciliation or settlement of disputes etc.; c. Origin of Christianity and Islam from Abraham as one father (Gen. 16:15 — 16, Gen. 21:1-3).

subtopics.name: Meaning of peaceful co-existence
objectives: Explain peaceful co-existence, i.e. living in peace with others (Matt. 5:21-25), with Bible instances: Esau and Jacob (Gen 31:1-11) (Gen. 13:1-8, 26:26-29), Philemon and Onesimus (Phil. 1:1-30), Isaac and Abimelech (Gen. 26-2 - 29)

subtopics.name: Ways of showing desire for peaceful co-existence
objectives: Demonstrate how people can show desire for peaceful co-existence, e.g. call for dialogue, tolerance, forgiveness, reconciliation or settlement of disputes etc.

subtopics.name: Origin of Christianity and Islam from Abraham
objectives: Trace the origin of Christianity and Islam from Abraham as one father (Gen. 16:15 — 16, Gen. 21:1-3)
